newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to publish airport privatization guidelines.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to publish airport privatization guidelines.

text.p: The guidelines for the auction to privatize Mexico's airports will be published in September, Communications and Transportation Ministry privatization coordinator Jorge Silberstein said on Monday.
"At the start of autumn we have to publish the general guidelines concerning the privatization... the invitations (to bid) will be more or less in September," Silberstein told reporters.
He said the auctions for the terminals will likely take place near the end of the year.
"At the end of the year or the start of next year will be the first auction," he said.
Under the most favorable conditons, "in the next year we will have privatized the 35 airports."
The ministry has said it will sell off 35 of the 57 terminals in regional packages.
Silberstein said in particular Spanish, Dutch, French, British and Canadian firms have showed interest in the airports.

Among the packets could be one that includes Mexico City airport, and another that includes 17 airports, among those Cancun and Monterrey. A third would include Guadalajara, Tijuana, Acapulco and Puerto Vallarta.
